serverInstructions: LoomLCI operates the user's local Windows environment with the user's normal permissions; it is not a sandbox. Prefer structured LoomLCI filesystem capabilities over shell commands when an equivalent operation exists. Use filesystem_view_image when visual inspection of a known local PNG, JPEG, or WebP is needed instead of reading or encoding the file manually. Use filesystem_read_pdf when text from a known local PDF is needed; it is page-bounded and does not perform OCR. Use filesystem_render_pdf_page when a specific PDF page must be inspected visually, including scans, diagrams, tables, or layout. Use python_execute for persistent in-session calculations, parsing, and transformations. Inside python_execute, import loom.fs for structured filesystem operations and loom.process for Loom-managed processes that should remain tied to the same WorkSession; loom.process supports one-shot runs plus durable pipes/terminal lifecycle, retained cursored output, stdin, resize, terminate and release. Durable processes created from Python are always SessionOwned and can survive python_reset until work_close/expiry or explicit release. For PNG/JPEG/WebP images generated in memory by Python, use loom.display_image(bytes|bytearray|memoryview); use filesystem_view_image for an image file that already exists and filesystem_render_pdf_page for an existing PDF page. Python image outputs are bounded to 4 outputs / 6 MiB raw aggregate and the full MCP result to 9 MiB; invalid image/final-payload failures happen after execution and preserve worker state, so do not automatically rerun code with possible side effects. If third-party Python packages are needed, call python_packages_prepare with the complete desired package set; when it reports workerRestartRequired=true, call python_reset before the next python_execute. Use top-level Process capabilities when an independent process is intentionally required. Use a work session when calls need a shared base directory or session-owned resources. Treat work and process handles as opaque values and pass them back unchanged. Close work sessions when their task is complete. Use Work Plan to organize non-trivial work with multiple meaningful phases, dependent actions, or checkpoints; skip it for simple lookups and short single-step tasks. On a newly created WorkSession, the plan starts empty at revision 0, so create the initial plan directly with work_plan_update and expectedRevision=0. Keep a concise plan with a few outcome-oriented steps and update it only at meaningful milestones. Prefer work_plan_patch for small changes to an existing plan; use work_plan_update for initial creation, reordering, full replacement, or clearing. Work Plan tracks logical progress only and does not execute or monitor real work. Preserve returned Work Plan step ids and revision; on conflict, reread the plan, reconcile, and retry. Loom does not auto-merge concurrent mutations.

tools.name: filesystem_apply_patch
tools.title: Apply file changes
tools.description: Applies structured file changes. write and replace are text operations with a 16 MiB text-content limit; delete and move operate on files without reading their contents, so they also work for large or binary files. Prefer this over shell commands for equivalent filesystem changes. Each call accepts up to 64 validated changes; dependent edits to the same path must be split into separate calls.

changes.description: One to 64 patch operations. write uses path+content; replace uses path+oldText+newText; delete uses path; move uses fromPath+toPath.

op.description: Operation: write, replace, delete, or move.

path.description: Target path for write, replace, or delete. Not used by move.

content.description: Complete text content for write. Required when op=write.

overwrite.description: For write or move, allow replacing an existing destination when true.

oldText.description: Exact non-empty text to replace. Required when op=replace.

newText.description: Replacement text. Required when op=replace and may be empty.

expectedOccurrences.description: Expected number of exact oldText matches for replace; the operation fails if the actual count differs.

fromPath.description: Source path for move. Required when op=move.

toPath.description: Destination path for move. Required when op=move.

workId.description: Optional work session handle used to resolve relative paths.

tools.name: filesystem_find_paths
tools.title: Find paths
tools.description: Finds files or directories by literal path/name fragments. If nextCursor is returned, pass it back as cursor with the same search/traversal inputs to continue without repeating matches; maxResults may change between pages. The cursor is opaque and becomes invalid if those inputs change or the filesystem changes at the resume point. Recursive traversal prunes common generated/infrastructure directories by default; explicitly targeting one of those directories as path still works. Directory matches may include childrenExcluded='generated' when default pruning skipped their children or childrenExcluded='excluded' when excludeDirectories skipped them; the field is omitted when children were traversed normally. Use this when searching for paths, filenames, or extensions; it does not inspect file contents. Use filesystem_search_text instead for text inside files. matchMode=suffix is useful for exact filename endings or extensions.

path.description: Root directory to search. May be absolute or relative to the work session base directory.

queries.description: One to 32 non-empty literal path queries. Multiple queries use OR semantics.

matchMode.description: Path matching strategy: substring matches anywhere in the relative path; suffix matches only path endings.

workId.description: Optional work session handle used to resolve relative paths.

includeGenerated.description: When false, recursive traversal prunes .git, .vs, .venv, __pycache__, bin, node_modules, obj, and .obsidian/plugins. Explicitly targeting one of those directories as path still traverses it.

excludeDirectories.description: Optional exact directory names to prune in addition to the defaults. Names are case-insensitive on Windows and are not glob patterns or paths.

maxResults.description: Maximum matching entries returned in this page.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from a previous filesystem_find_paths call with the same search/traversal inputs. Omit for the first page; maxResults may differ between pages.

tools.name: filesystem_list_tree
tools.title: List directory tree
tools.description: Lists a bounded recursive directory tree. Use this to discover project structure when exact paths are not yet known. If nextCursor is returned, pass it back as cursor with the same traversal inputs to continue without repeating entries; maxEntries may change between pages. The cursor is opaque and becomes invalid if traversal parameters change or the filesystem changes at the resume point. Recursive traversal prunes common generated/infrastructure directories by default while still showing the directory itself; explicitly targeting one of those directories as path still works. A returned directory may include childrenExcluded='generated' when default pruning skipped its children or childrenExcluded='excluded' when excludeDirectories skipped them; the field is omitted when children were traversed normally. It does not read file contents; prefer filesystem_find_paths for name/path lookup, filesystem_search_text for content search, and filesystem_read_files once exact files are known.

path.description: Directory path. May be absolute or relative to the work session base directory.

workId.description: Optional work session handle used to resolve relative paths.

includeGenerated.description: When false, recursive traversal prunes .git, .vs, .venv, __pycache__, bin, node_modules, obj, and .obsidian/plugins. Explicitly targeting one of those directories as path still traverses it.

excludeDirectories.description: Optional exact directory names to prune in addition to the defaults. Names are case-insensitive on Windows and are not glob patterns or paths.

maxEntries.description: Maximum entries returned in this page.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from a previous filesystem_list_tree call with the same traversal inputs. Omit for the first page; maxEntries may differ between pages.

tools.name: filesystem_manage_directory
tools.title: Manage directory
tools.description: Creates a directory including missing parents, or deletes one existing empty directory. This is not recursive deletion and does not edit file contents.

workId.description: Optional work session handle used to resolve relative paths.

tools.name: filesystem_read_files
tools.title: Read text files
tools.description: Reads known text files, optionally by 1-based line range. Large files can be read in bounded ranges by supplying limit; unbounded whole-file reads over 16 MiB are rejected. MCP responses are capped at a safe 9 MiB serialized budget, so large results must be split into smaller line ranges or separate calls. Each file result reports hasMoreBefore and hasMoreAfter so partial ranges are explicit without implying transport truncation. Use this when exact file paths are already known; prefer filesystem_search_text when you first need to locate content. Multiple files can be read in one call.

files.description: One to 32 files to read. Offset is the optional 1-based starting line and limit is the optional maximum line count.

path.description: File path to read. May be absolute or relative to the work session base directory.

limit.description: Optional maximum number of lines to return.

workId.description: Optional work session handle used to resolve relative paths.

hasMoreBefore.description: True when the file has lines before startLine that were not returned.

hasMoreAfter.description: True when the file has lines after endLine that were not returned.

tools.name: filesystem_read_pdf
tools.title: Read PDF text
tools.description: Extracts bounded text from a known local PDF using a crash-isolated worker. Pages are 1-based and results are paginated by page. PDFs over 64 MiB are rejected. This tool does not perform OCR or render pages, so scanned/image-only PDFs may return little or no text.

path.description: PDF path. May be absolute or relative to the work session base directory.

workId.description: Optional work session handle used to resolve relative paths.

maxPages.description: Maximum number of pages to read in this call.

tools.name: filesystem_render_pdf_page
tools.title: Render PDF page
tools.description: Renders one 1-based page from a known local PDF to PNG using a crash-isolated worker. Use this for scanned/image-only PDFs, diagrams, tables, or visual layout that text extraction cannot capture. The image preserves aspect ratio inside maxWidth/maxHeight. PDFs over 64 MiB are rejected; rendered PNG and MCP visual payload limits are enforced.

path.description: PDF path. May be absolute or relative to the work session base directory.

workId.description: Optional work session handle used to resolve relative paths.

tools.name: filesystem_search_text
tools.title: Search text
tools.description: Searches one to 32 literal text queries in a single filesystem traversal with OR semantics. Results are grouped by matching physical line: each line appears once with queryMatches identifying every query that matched and its first 1-based UTF-16 column. Matching lines and context are bounded excerpts; textStartColumn/textTruncated and context excerpt metadata indicate when text was shortened. maxResults limits matching lines per page. Search streams files of any size and scans up to about 64 MiB per page; if nextCursor is returned, pass it back as cursor with the same search/traversal inputs to continue. maxResults may change between pages. resultLimitReached and scanLimitReached explain why the current page stopped. Files classified as binary by an initial decoded-prefix NUL heuristic are skipped and reported by skippedBinaryFileCount/skippedBinaryFiles. Recursive traversal pruning matches the other filesystem discovery tools. Use filesystem_read_files after locating files that need fuller exact context.

path.description: File or directory path to search. May be absolute or relative to the work session base directory.

queries.description: One to 32 non-empty literal text queries. Multiple queries use OR semantics and are searched in one traversal; this is not regex.

workId.description: Optional work session handle used to resolve relative paths.

includeGenerated.description: When false, recursive traversal prunes .git, .vs, .venv, __pycache__, bin, node_modules, obj, and .obsidian/plugins. Explicitly targeting one of those directories as path still traverses it.

excludeDirectories.description: Optional exact directory names to prune in addition to the defaults. Names are case-insensitive on Windows and are not glob patterns or paths.

maxResults.description: Maximum matching lines returned in this page across all queries.

contextLines.description: Context lines returned before and after each match.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from a previous filesystem_search_text call with the same search/traversal inputs. Omit for the first page; maxResults may differ between pages.

tools.name: filesystem_view_image
tools.title: View local image
tools.description: Reads one known local PNG, JPEG, or WebP file and returns it as image content for visual inspection. Use this when the model needs to see an image rather than read it as text or base64. The path may be absolute or relative to a work session base directory. The file is returned unchanged: this tool does not resize, convert, edit, or OCR the image. Images over 6 MiB or whose MCP result would exceed the visual payload budget are rejected.

path.description: Image path. May be absolute or relative to the work session base directory.

workId.description: Optional work session handle used to resolve relative paths.

tools.name: process_read
tools.title: Read process output
tools.description: Reads retained process output non-destructively and also returns current process state. For an exited or terminated process, a successful read refreshes the post-exit retention window and returns the new retentionExpiresAt inside process. Pipe-based processes expose separate stdout/stderr streams; terminal processes expose one terminal stream containing raw UTF-8-decoded text plus VT/ANSI sequences. Cursors are absolute UTF-16 positions: reuse each returned nextCursor to continue exactly after the last returned text, even when maxChars cuts through a producer read. maxChars limits only this response, not capture; a read may exceed it by one UTF-16 code unit rather than split a surrogate pair. Each active stream is spooled to temporary storage up to a 64 MiB retention quota; if that quota is exceeded, retentionLimitReached is true and retainedUntilCursor/observedUntilCursor make the omitted tail explicit.

stdoutCursor.description: Next stdout cursor for a pipe-based process, or 0. Must remain 0 for terminal processes.

stderrCursor.description: Next stderr cursor for a pipe-based process, or 0. Must remain 0 for terminal processes.

terminalCursor.description: Next terminal cursor for a terminal process, or 0. Must remain 0 for pipe-based processes.

maxChars.description: Maximum total characters returned across the active process output streams.

tools.name: process_release
tools.title: Release process handle
tools.description: Explicitly releases a retained Loom process handle after the root process has exited or been terminated. This permanently discards retained process state and output, closes process/Job/pipe or terminal resources, and may terminate descendants that are still attached to the Loom Job. Read any final output you need before calling this tool. This does not stop a live process: starting, running, or terminating processes return conflict; use process_terminate first when the process should be stopped. Releasing an already closed or expired handle is idempotent while its tombstone is retained.

processHandle.description: Process handle returned by process_start. The root process must already be exited or terminated.

tools.name: process_resize
tools.title: Resize process terminal
tools.description: Resizes a running terminal-mode process. This is only supported for processes started with ioMode=terminal; pipe-based processes do not have terminal dimensions.

tools.name: process_run
tools.title: Run short process
tools.description: Runs a short, non-interactive pipe-based process and waits for it to finish, returning exit code plus bounded stdout/stderr in one call. Use this for quick commands such as git status or --version lookups. A non-zero exit code is still a successful LoomLCI tool result. This tool does not return a process handle and cannot be continued, written to, resized, or used as a background/terminal process; use process_start for those cases. timeoutSeconds covers the whole run and cancellation/timeout cleans up the process tree. maxOutputChars is the total response budget shared by stdout and stderr.

executable.description: Executable path or executable name resolved by Windows. This tool does not infer or insert a shell.

arguments.description: Arguments passed directly to the executable as an argument array.

workingDirectory.description: Optional working directory. Relative paths require a work session with a base directory.

workId.description: Optional work session handle. Keeps the session leased during execution and enables relative workingDirectory resolution.

environment.description: Environment variable overrides. A null value removes that variable.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum duration of the whole one-shot run in seconds.

maxOutputChars.description: Maximum total characters returned across stdout and stderr.

tools.name: process_start
tools.title: Start process
tools.description: Starts one executable directly, without shell parsing, and returns a durable process handle immediately. ioMode=pipes is the default for normal automation with separate stdout/stderr; ioMode=terminal requests a real Windows terminal for shells, REPLs, TUIs, or programs that require console semantics. Pass arguments as an explicit array. For cmd.exe syntax such as pipes, redirection, &&, or built-ins, explicitly start cmd.exe with /d /s /c; for PowerShell syntax, explicitly start powershell.exe or pwsh.exe. After the process reaches a terminal state, the handle and retained output remain available for the reported postExitRetentionSeconds; successful process_status/process_read calls refresh that post-exit retention window. A live process does not expire merely because it is not polled. Use process_read when output matters and process_status when only state or exit metadata is needed.

executable.description: Executable path or executable name resolved by Windows. This tool does not infer or insert a shell.

arguments.description: Arguments passed directly to the executable as an argument array. Do not apply shell quoting or combine multiple shell tokens into one argument unless the target executable itself expects that.

workingDirectory.description: Optional working directory. Relative paths require a work session with a base directory.

workId.description: Work session handle. Required for session-owned processes.

independent.description: If true, the live process is not cleaned up when the work session closes. It remains Loom-managed: after the root process reaches a terminal state, post-exit retention still applies, and expiry releases retained output plus any descendants still in the process Job.

environment.description: Environment variable overrides. A null value removes that variable.

ioMode.description: Process I/O mode. pipes keeps separate stdout/stderr and is the default; terminal requests ConPTY terminal semantics.

terminalColumns.description: Optional initial terminal width in columns. Only valid with ioMode=terminal; defaults to 80 there.

terminalRows.description: Optional initial terminal height in rows. Only valid with ioMode=terminal; defaults to 24 there.

tools.name: process_status
tools.title: Get process status
tools.description: Returns only the current state, I/O mode, exit metadata, and post-exit retention deadline for a Loom process handle. For an exited or terminated process, a successful call refreshes the post-exit retention window and returns the new retentionExpiresAt. Running processes do not expire for lack of polling. Use this when output is irrelevant; use process_read instead when process output is needed because process_read also includes current process state.

tools.name: process_terminate
tools.title: Terminate process
tools.description: Terminates a Loom-managed process and its descendant process tree. Use this only when the process should be stopped rather than allowed to exit normally. Termination itself is idempotent: calling it again after the process has already exited or been terminated succeeds without changing the final process state. A successful call also refreshes the post-exit retention window, so the overall tool call is not annotated as idempotent.

tools.name: process_write
tools.title: Write process stdin
tools.description: Writes text verbatim to a running process input. For pipe-based processes this writes stdin; for terminal processes this writes the ConPTY input stream, including control characters or VT sequences. To send Ctrl+C to a terminal without terminating the terminal process, write \u0003 (ETX). No newline is appended automatically; include it in text when the target expects Enter or a line terminator.

text.description: Text to write verbatim to the process input. Include newline or control characters when required by the target process. For terminal Ctrl+C, write \u0003 (ETX).

tools.name: python_execute
tools.title: Execute Python
tools.description: Executes Python code in the persistent Python worker owned by a work session. The first call lazily provisions/starts the private CPython runtime; later calls in the same work session reuse globals, imports, cwd changes, and other in-process state. Use this for local calculations, parsing, transformations, and short stateful Python workflows. Inside the worker, import loom, loom.fs, or loom.process to use LoomLCI capabilities against the same work session. loom.fs provides structured filesystem operations (list/search/read/patch/directories/textual PDF). loom.process provides Loom-managed run/start/status/read/write/resize/terminate/release with Job Objects, retained output and terminal support; durable processes created there are always session-owned. Normal bridge failures raise loom.LoomError and do not discard the worker. Use loom.display_image(bytes|bytearray|memoryview) for PNG, JPEG, or WebP images generated in memory during this Python execution. Up to 4 image outputs are allowed with 6 MiB raw aggregate, and the complete MCP result (text, metadata, and images) must fit a 9 MiB serialized response budget. Use filesystem_view_image for image files that already exist and filesystem_render_pdf_page for existing PDF pages instead of loading those files into Python just to display them. Invalid image format or a final result over the MCP budget is reported after Python has already completed with executionCompleted=true; worker globals and side effects remain, so do not automatically retry the same code. There is no interactive stdin in this version: input() receives EOF. A normal Python exception is a successful tool call with result.status='exception' and can preserve images emitted before the exception; infrastructure failures, cancellation, and timeouts are tool errors. timeoutSeconds covers the whole invocation, including lazy runtime provisioning/startup. On timeout, cancellation, crash, or broken protocol the worker is discarded, so the next call starts with a fresh namespace. maxOutputChars applies independently to stdout and stderr and counts Unicode code points; truncation does not stop code execution. Code is limited to 256 KiB when encoded as strict UTF-8.

workId.description: Work session handle returned by work_create. Python state is scoped to this session.

code.description: Python source code to execute. Maximum 256 KiB when encoded as strict UTF-8.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum duration in seconds for the entire Python invocation, including lazy provisioning/startup.

maxOutputChars.description: Maximum Unicode code points returned for each of stdout and stderr. Execution continues after this response limit is reached.

tools.name: python_packages_prepare
tools.title: Prepare Python packages
tools.description: Prepares the complete desired third-party package set for a work session using LoomLCI's private Python runtime and package store. Packages are resolved only from the official PyPI index, installed from wheels only, locked to exact versions with hashes, and kept outside the immutable CPython runtime. Pass the full desired direct-package set on every call; an empty array switches the session back to base Python with no third-party environment. Package names and optional exact versions are structured inputs; direct URLs, Git/VCS, local paths, editable installs, private indexes and source builds are not supported. Prepared environments are reusable across work sessions. If a Python worker is already alive with a different environment, the call succeeds with workerRestartRequired=true; call python_reset before the next python_execute. Preparing packages can access the network and may take substantially longer than a normal python_execute on first use.

workId.description: Work session handle returned by work_create.

packages.description: Complete desired set of zero to 32 direct PyPI packages for this work session.

name.description: PyPI project name. Direct URLs, paths, Git/VCS and requirement options are not accepted.

version.description: Optional exact package version. Omit to resolve the current compatible stable version.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum duration in seconds for resolution/download/install.

tools.name: python_reset
tools.title: Reset Python session
tools.description: Discards the persistent Python worker and namespace owned by the work session. This is idempotent: it succeeds when no worker exists. The next python_execute starts a fresh worker. This is not an interrupt command; if an execution is already active, reset waits for that resource lease to finish before disposing the worker.

workId.description: Work session handle whose Python worker should be discarded.

tools.name: work_close
tools.title: Close work session
tools.description: Closes a work session and cleans up its session-owned resources. After close, session-owned resource handles are closed and can no longer be inspected with tools such as process_status or process_read, so read any final state or output you need before closing. Call this when the task using that session is complete; independent resources are not owned by the session.

workId.description: The work session handle returned by work_create.

tools.name: work_create
tools.title: Create work session
tools.description: Creates a work session for calls that need a shared base directory or session-owned resources. Use it before relative-path operations or session-owned process_start calls; stateless operations with fully explicit absolute paths do not require one. Inactive work sessions expire automatically after the idle timeout reported in the result; active invocations keep the session alive.

baseDirectory.description: Optional base directory used to resolve relative paths. This is context, not a security boundary.

label.description: Optional human-readable label for the work session.

tools.name: work_plan_get
tools.title: Get work plan
tools.description: Reads the current logical Work Plan when resuming or inspecting an existing non-trivial work session, or before reconciling a conflict from work_plan_update/work_plan_patch. A newly created WorkSession always starts with an empty plan at revision 0, so do not call this only to initialize a new plan; work_plan_update can start it directly with expectedRevision=0. The plan tracks agent-visible progress only; it does not execute, observe, or synchronize Process, Python, Filesystem, or other real work. A successful read refreshes the work session idle timeout.

workId.description: Work session handle returned by work_create.

tools.name: work_plan_patch
tools.title: Patch work plan
tools.description: Atomically applies one to 32 small changes to the current Work Plan without resending untouched steps. Use add to append a new step, update to change text/status of one existing step while preserving omitted fields and position, and remove to delete one existing step. Preserve opaque step ids exactly. The whole patch uses expectedRevision compare-and-swap: on conflict no changes are applied, so reread, reconcile, and retry; Loom does not auto-merge concurrent patches. A successful call increments revision once and returns the complete normalized snapshot, including ids assigned to added steps. Use work_plan_update instead when you need initial creation, reordering, complete replacement, or clearing.

workId.description: Work session handle returned by work_create.

expectedRevision.description: Expected Work Plan revision from the latest observed snapshot or successful mutation.

changes.description: One to 32 atomic patch changes. add uses text plus optional status; update uses id plus text and/or status; remove uses id only.

op.description: Patch operation: add, update, or remove.

id.description: Existing opaque step id. Required for update/remove and forbidden for add.

text.description: Optional short single-line step text. Required for add; optional for update; forbidden for remove.

status.description: Optional logical step status. add defaults to pending when omitted.

tools.name: work_plan_update
tools.title: Create or replace work plan
tools.description: Creates or atomically replaces the complete logical Work Plan for non-trivial work. Use this for initial creation, reordering, full reconciliation, replacement, or clearing; prefer work_plan_patch for small milestone changes to an existing plan. On a newly created WorkSession, start directly with expectedRevision=0; otherwise use the revision from the latest work_plan_get or successful mutation. On conflict, reread the plan, reconcile, and retry. For a new step omit id or pass null; for an existing step preserve its opaque id exactly. Omitting an existing id removes that step; an empty steps array clears the plan. Multiple active and waiting steps are allowed. This tool only changes logical plan state; it does not execute steps or alter Process, Python, Filesystem, or other resources.

workId.description: Work session handle returned by work_create.

expectedRevision.description: Expected Work Plan revision. Use 0 immediately after creating a new WorkSession; otherwise use the latest observed revision.

steps.description: Complete replacement list of zero to 32 logical steps. Prefer a concise set of outcome-oriented steps.

text.description: Short single-line step text. Maximum 512 Unicode code points.

id.description: Existing opaque step id returned by Loom. Omit or pass null to create a new step.
